High Bridge Trail State Park stretches for 31 miles through
LIA Appomattox, Cumberland, Nottoway and Prince Edward counties and
the towns of Burkeville, Farmville, Pamplin City, Prospect and Rice. The
7 trail, once a rail bed, is wide, level and generally flat with a surface of
616 finely crushed limestone. The centerpiece is the majestic High Bridge.
Built in 1853, the bridge is more than 2,400 feet long and towers 125
feet above the Appomattox River.

Virginia is home to 855 miles of the U.S. Bicycle Route
System. Established by the federal government in 1982, the
Virginia sections of U.S. Bicycle Routes 76 and 1 cross the
250
76 state from east to west, and north to south respectively. Just
south of Waynesboro near Afton Mountain, USBR 76 runs
l
1 along the Blue Ridge Parkway for 25 miles, overlooking the
Shenandoah Valley to the west and Nelson County’s Rockfish
Valley to the east.
The Blue Ridge Parkway is a 469-mile scenic route that
runs through Virginia and North Carolina. It is the most
visited of all sites in the National Park system, and is popular
35 among bicyclists due to its limited access and lower traffic
levels compared to most public highways. Traveling the Blue
Ridge Parkway by bicycle is an unforgettable experience, but
requires planning and caution. Temperatures can change
rapidly with elevations ranging from 650 feet to more than
6
6,000 feet. Avoid the parkway during fog and take care
when traveling through any of the 27 tunnels along the
route. Bicycles are only allowed on paved roadways.

From the Hiwassee trestle south of Pulaski, the trail begins a steady climb southwest to Fries
Junction, and then splits to provide access to the towns of Fries and Galax. Many access
points provide entry to the trail, which is the centerpiece of this 765-acre park that only
averages a width of about 80 feet. Campgrounds and facilities are available for a variety of
visitors including cyclists, hikers, equestrians and paddlers.
Those with an adventurous spirit can participate in the New River Trail Challenge, a triathlon
with segments for mountain biking, canoeing and running.

Virginia welcomes cyclists! Traveling on your bicycle
through Virginia offers a unique perspective of a
landscape that changes dramatically as you move
across the state. From the Atlantic coastal areas to the
mountains, there is much to see and experience in the
commonwealth. With historic sites, State Parks, Civil War
battlefields, wineries and so many other attractions,
there is something for everyone to enjoy. Whether you
plan a leisurely ride on the Capital Trail, take a few days
to trek through southwest Virginia, or head out on the
Blue Ridge Parkway, there are hundreds of bike-friendly
sites to experience.
Additional information can be found online at
http://www.virginiadot.org/bikemap.

The Virginia Creeper Trail is a multipurpose trail running 34
miles along a former rail bed with geography that ranges from
mountains to valleys. It owes its popularity to outstanding scenery,
starting with the Blue Ridge to the east and meandering westward
through the Valley and Ridge section of Virginia. Take two days
to see the entire trail, or ride the length of the trail from Whitetop
to Abingdon in a single, day-long excursion.
